items.title: ReconLegacy Runbook (v3.2)
items.text:
ReconLegacy Runbook (v3.2)
Owner: Technology. Last updated Fri 2026-07-10 by Priya Raman.

Purpose
ReconLegacy is the end-of-day reconciliation batch. It matches settled trades from SettlementEngine against GLCore balances and publishes a break report to #recon for the Operations reconciliation team. It is a set of Perl batch jobs on a single Oracle 11g host (reconprd01). It is a legacy system. Treat changes conservatively and test against the UAT schema first.

Schedule
The master wrapper (recon_master.pl) runs from cron at 02:15 ET, Monday through Saturday. The Saturday run covers Friday activity. Normal completion is between 04:45 and 05:30. The break report must be posted to #recon by 06:30 ET. If it has not posted by 06:00, start triage.

Job Steps
Step 1, load_settle.pl: picks up the SettlementEngine extract files from the inbound SFTP drop. Expects the trade file and the cash movements file, both stamped with the business date.
Step 2, load_gl.pl: pulls GLCore end-of-day balances through the read-only DB link.
Step 3, match_core.pl: runs the matching rules (trade ref, CUSIP/ISIN, quantity, net amount tolerance) and writes into RECON.BREAK_HIST.
Step 4, load_fx.pl: loads the FX rate table from the PricingSvc end-of-day snapshot. It then re-values non-USD legs and re-runs the match for those legs.
Step 5, publish.pl: renders the break report and posts it to #recon through the webhook. It also archives a CSV to the shared recon folder.

Each step writes to /var/log/recon/<step>_<YYYYMMDD>.log and records its status in RECON.JOB_STATUS.

Common Failures

1. Late settlement file
Symptom: step 1 log shows "waiting for settle extract". After 90 minutes it exits with RC=12.
Action: confirm with Operations (Settlements) that SettlementEngine has finished its EOD run. Once the files land, restart from step 1:
  recon_master.pl --from-step 1
If the files are for the right date but the names are wrong, do not rename them by hand. Escalate to the SettlementEngine on-call.

2. Oracle tablespace full (ORA-01653)
Symptom: step 3 aborts with "ORA-01653: unable to extend table RECON.BREAK_HIST". This usually happens after high-volume days or at quarter end.
Action: check free space in RECON_DATA with the dba_free_space query in scripts/space_check.sql. Add a datafile or resize the existing one, following the DBA standard in the Oracle wiki. Do not enable autoextend without a max size. Then restart from step 3:
  recon_master.pl --from-step 3
If space is fine, purge BREAK_HIST partitions older than 13 months using purge_hist.pl. That is the retention policy agreed with Compliance.

3. FX rate table not loaded from the PricingSvc snapshot
Symptom: the report shows a cluster of breaks, all on FX or non-USD trades, with amount differences that look like a rate mismatch. The step 4 log shows "snapshot not found" or a snapshot timestamp from the prior day.
Action: confirm that the PricingSvc EOD snapshot has published. PricingSvc depends on MarketDataFeed, so check #incidents for feed issues first. Then re-run step 4 only:
  recon_master.pl --step 4
and re-publish:
  recon_master.pl --step 5
Step 4 has a stale-price guard. If the snapshot is older than the business date, the job aborts on purpose instead of valuing breaks at old rates.

Re-running a Prior Business Date
Use the --asof flag, for example:
  recon_master.pl --asof 2026-07-09
This reloads that date's inputs and overwrites that date's rows in BREAK_HIST. Tell #recon before you run it, because analysts may already be working those breaks.

Not Covered in This Runbook
The FX adjustment module (fx_adj.pm, called inside step 4) and the month-end manual override process are not documented here. Both rely on hand-maintained config and on judgment calls made at month end. Do not change either without talking to me first.

Contacts
Primary: Priya Raman (Technology)
Business users: Tasha Greene, Reconciliation (Operations)
Escalation: Sam Okafor, Director of Engineering
Morning all, I'm looking at 14 breaks this morning and every single one is an FX trade. Amounts are off by what looks like a rate difference. Is ReconLegacy broken again? @Priya Raman

Not broken, just late. The FX rate table didn't load from the PricingSvc snapshot in time, so step 4 valued those legs at yesterday's rates. I re-ran step 4 and re-published, so the 14 FX breaks should clear once you refresh. Shout if any are still there.
Hey, the recon report never arrived this morning. I'm guessing it's related to yesterday's PricingSvc incident? Nothing posted for Friday's business date as far as I can see.

Yep, same root cause. I re-ran the batch manually with --asof 2026-08-14 and the report just posted. Step 4 has a stale-price guard: when the PricingSvc snapshot is older than the business date, the job aborts rather than valuing breaks at old FX rates. Yesterday's snapshot published late after the incident, so the 02:15 run correctly bailed out.

items.title: ReconLegacy nightly job failed: ORA-01653 unable to extend table
items.text:
The nightly ReconLegacy batch failed overnight and no break report was posted to #recon for business date 2026-08-26. The shared folder has no CSV either. The status page shows step 3 (match_core) in FAILED state. The error I can see in the job status is: ORA-01653: unable to extend table RECON.BREAK_HIST in tablespace RECON_DATA. Yesterday was a heavy settlement day. We need the report before the 09:00 breaks review with Settlements. Please prioritize.

--- Comment by Priya Raman ---
Picking this up. I confirmed that steps 1 and 2 completed normally, so the SettlementEngine extracts and GLCore balances loaded fine. Step 3 aborted at 03:41 ET when BREAK_HIST couldn't extend. RECON_DATA was at 99.6% used. Yesterday's volume plus the month-end ramp pushed it over.

--- Comment by Priya Raman ---
Tablespace fix: I added a new datafile to RECON_DATA with a capped max size, following the DBA standard. Autoextend is on but bounded, not unlimited. Free space is now about 38%. I also ran purge_hist.pl for the partitions that were past the 13-month retention window, which freed a bit more. I'm kicking off a manual re-run with recon_master.pl --from-step 3, since the earlier loads are good.

--- Comment by Priya Raman ---
The re-run completed cleanly. Step 3 finished at 07:52, step 4 loaded the FX rates from the PricingSvc snapshot without issue, and step 5 posted the break report to #recon at 08:04. The CSV is archived. Tasha, the break count looks in line with a normal heavy day, but let me know if anything looks off. I'm adding a tablespace usage alert at 85% so we see this coming next time.

--- Comment by Tasha Greene ---
Got the report, thanks Priya. The numbers look sane and we're good for the 09:00 review.

--- Comment by Priya Raman ---
Resolving as of 08:10 ET. Root cause was RECON_DATA tablespace exhaustion. It was fixed by adding a datafile and purging out-of-retention partitions, followed by a manual re-run from step 3. Runbook section 2 (ORA-01653) was followed as written.
